newsitem.title: UK: United Utilities bucks weaker utilities trend.
newsitem.headline: United Utilities bucks weaker utilities trend.

text.p: Shares in United Utilities bounced back from earlier weakness in the sector on Tuesday to be the only water stock in positive territory, helped by upbeat broker comment, dealers said.
By 1345 GMT the shares were up 1p at 575p after earlier suffering a 26p fall in a knee-jerk reaction to unexpected news that the UK Treasury was to scrap tax credits on share buybacks.

Market sources said upbeat broker comment on United Utilities had fuelled the recovery in its share price. Analysts at NatWest and SGST were said to be positive on the stock, but were not immediately available to comment.
Analysts at SBC Warburg were prompted to repeat their "buy' stance on the stock after United announced a higher than expected sale price for its Process Equipment arm yesterday.
Warburg also gave a share price target of 650p, market sources said.
Among others in the sector, East Midlands Electricity, Yorkshire Electricity and London Electric, seen as the most likely to have considered buyback schemes, suffered the sharpest losses.
